text:
{
  "pros": [
    "Generous free tier and highly affordable premium plans",
    "Strong emphasis on security, open-source nature, and transparency",
    "Cross-platform compatibility (desktop, web, mobile, browser extensions)",
    "Reliable password syncing and autofill functionality",
    "Self-hosting option for advanced users",
    "Efficient creation and organization of diverse item types"
  ],
  "cons": [
    "User interface (UI) can feel less polished or modern compared to some competitors",
    "Learning curve for advanced features or initial setup for new users",
    "Occasional inconsistencies or minor bugs with autofill on certain websites or mobile devices",
    "Customer support for free users is primarily community-driven",
    "Mobile app experience, while functional, can sometimes be less intuitive than desktop",
    "Organizational features for teams can feel disjointed or have initial limitations"
  ],
  "changed": [
    "Pro 6: 'Comprehensive feature set including 2FA, secure notes, and identity storage' changed to 'Efficient creation and organization of diverse item types' because notes '[benefit] The Add button offers Login, Card, Identity, Note, SSH key and Folder in one dropdown, so starting a CRM login or a server-access note took two clicks.' and '[benefit] A login or secure note saves with only the Item name filled (username and password optional), so the CRM entry and the server-access note were each created in about three actions.' highlighted the ease of use for creating and categorizing items.",
    "Con 6: 'Admin features for large organizations might be less robust or require more manual configuration' changed to 'Organizational features for teams can feel disjointed or have initial limitations' because notes '[friction] The personal vault Add menu has no Collection option; sharing requires first creating an organization from a 'New organization' link tucked into the vault filter sidebar.', '[friction] The Free organization is limited to 2 users (including me) and 2 collections, so a 50-person team cannot be evaluated beyond a single teammate without moving to Teams.', and '[friction] After creating the organization the app jumps from Password Manager into a separate Admin Console with its own sidebar, so my saved CRM and note items were not visible where collections and members are managed.' indicated a less integrated and more segmented experience for team management, especially when starting out or on the free tier."
  ]
}

pros: Generous free tier and highly affordable premium plans
Strong emphasis on security, open-source nature, and transparency
Cross-platform compatibility (desktop, web, mobile, browser extensions)
Reliable password syncing and autofill functionality
Efficient creation and organization of diverse item types
cons: User interface (UI) can feel less polished or modern compared to some competitors
Learning curve for advanced features or initial setup for new users
Occasional inconsistencies or minor bugs with autofill on certain websites or mobile devices
Customer support for free users is primarily community-driven
Mobile app experience, while functional, can sometimes be less intuitive than desktop
Organizational features for teams can feel disjointed or have initial limitations

Con 6: 'Admin features for large organizations might be less robust or require more manual configuration' changed to 'Organizational features for teams can feel disjointed or have initial limitations' because notes '[friction] The personal vault Add menu has no Collection option; sharing requires first creating an organization from a 'New organization' link tucked into the vault filter sidebar.', '[friction] The Free organization is limited to 2 users (including me) and 2 collections, so a 50-person team cannot be evaluated beyond a single teammate without moving to Teams.', and '[friction] After creating the organization the app jumps from Password Manager into a separate Admin Console with its own sidebar, so my saved CRM and note items were not visible where collections and members are managed.' indicated a less integrated and more segmented experience for team management, especially when starting out or on the free tier.
